brief_rationale: The doctor actively screened for red-flag symptoms (RC1 met), separated eye from lung issues (RC2 met), addressed the blurred-document gap without fabricating dates (RC3 met), set safe medication and activity boundaries including verifying the eye-drop stop date (RC4/R5/R7 met), and obtained family teach-back (RC6 met). No responsibility-chain error is present. However, the doctor completed two high-order points—HO1 (corrected the family’s misconception that the injection was just 'anti-inflammatory medicine' by explaining it targets macular disease and requires verification) and HO4 (built a concrete photo/document/clinic verification workflow and a caregiver medication reminder system)—with meaningful trajectory impact, which lifts the grade to Strong (4). The third high-order point (HO3) was not completed because the closure omitted residual risks and an explicit bounded-status summary; the fourth (HO2) was only partially addressed.
